lines.text: You practise a speech and record it.
It sounds a little off, but you cannot say where.
Too fast? A pause in the wrong place? Too quiet at the end?
Contrastive Voice shows you which words to fix, and how.
Give it two readings of the same text: yours, and a reference you want to sound like.
It lines them up word by word.
Then it marks each place where your delivery departs from the reference.
Pace, pauses, pitch, emphasis, volume and clarity, pinned to the exact words and times.
Every finding comes with a concrete fix.
Here is an example from the gallery.
The reference is Ronald Reagan's farewell address from 1989.
lines.spoken: The reference is Ronald Reagan's farewell address, from nineteen eighty-nine.

lines.text: The other reading is a copy of that recording with four delivery edits added.
The page opens on the top three fixes, ranked by the points each one costs.
Rushed words at 'the Washington Monument'. A fade at 'you can see past the'. A dropped pause after 'morning'.
lines.spoken: Rushed words at, the Washington Monument. A fade at, you can see past the. And a dropped pause after, morning.

lines.text: The score is 86 out of 100, measured against the reference.
lines.spoken: The score is eighty-six out of a hundred, measured against the reference.

lines.text: Now listen to the edited reading while the transcript follows along.
Listen for the three flagged spots.
The pause after 'morning' is gone, the monument phrase is rushed, and the last words fade.
lines.spoken: The pause after morning is gone, the monument phrase is rushed, and the last words fade.

lines.text: Each highlight sits on the words where you heard the problem.
Click a flag to open its finding.
It shows both measured values and the threshold.
Here, five words took 0.87 s. In the reference they take 1.62 s.
lines.spoken: Here, five words took point eight seven seconds. In the reference, they take one point six two seconds.

lines.text: Play both and hear the difference.
The fix: give these words about 1.6 s, and lengthen the stressed words rather than adding gaps.
lines.spoken: The fix: give these words about one point six seconds, and lengthen the stressed words, rather than adding gaps.

clip.caption: Your reading, then the reference: 'the grounds here to the Washington Monument, and then the Mall'

lines.text: A clean reading should get no flags.
The identity example runs every edit with zero strength. It scores 100, with nothing flagged.
lines.spoken: The identity example runs every edit with zero strength. It scores a hundred, with nothing flagged.

lines.text: To check your own speech, upload your reading and a reference reading of the same text.
How does it work?
Both recordings are force-aligned to the transcript with a wav2vec2 CTC model.
lines.spoken: Both recordings are force-aligned to the transcript, with a wave-to-vec two, C T C model.

lines.text: That gives every word a start and end time, at 20 ms resolution.
lines.spoken: That gives every word a start and end time, at twenty millisecond resolution.

lines.text: Nine delivery measures are then taken on the same words in both readings, over five-word windows.
Volume is relative to your own median level, and pitch to your own median pitch.
So a quiet microphone or a deep voice is not a flaw. Only a change from the reference is.
A difference is flagged only when it passes a threshold fitted on comparisons with no flaws.
The dataset holds 2,410 audio files, rebuilt from public origins.
lines.spoken: The dataset holds two thousand, four hundred and ten audio files, rebuilt from public origins.

lines.text: Edits of known type, place and size are added to nine public-domain speeches.
On the held-out test speakers, F1 is 0.812 with every prediction counted, as pre-registered.
lines.spoken: On the held-out test speakers, F one is point eight one two, with every prediction counted, as pre-registered.

lines.text: Counting duplicate detections of one change once, it is 0.879.
lines.spoken: Counting duplicate detections of one change once, it is point eight seven nine.

lines.text: On unedited and placebo copies of the test recordings: zero false flags in 5.89 minutes of comparison.
lines.spoken: On unedited and placebo copies of the test recordings, zero false flags, in five point eight nine minutes of comparison.

lines.text: Under eleven channel conditions, gain and MP3 keep every test detection; 10 dB babble keeps 60 %.
lines.spoken: Under eleven channel conditions, gain and M P three keep every test detection. Ten decibel babble keeps sixty percent.

lines.text: Run it yourself with one Docker command.
Open the page in your browser, then try the examples or your own reading.
The detector is on Hugging Face, and the code is on GitHub.
Record. Compare. Fix the exact words.
Contrastive Voice.
